notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT draft: it is shorter than the prophet drafts, stays inside the event's own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state; the prophet stories (content/stories) are not repeated here. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

chapters.title_en: Glory to Him who took His servant

claims.statement_en: Glory to Him who took His servant by night from the inviolable mosque to the farthest mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed.
The purpose given is to show him some of Our signs.
He is the Hearing, the Seeing.

chapters.summary_md: The ayah gives glory to Him who took His servant by night from the inviolable mosque to the farthest mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed [c1]. It says the purpose was to show him some of Our signs [c2].
chapters.body_md: The ayah gives glory to Him who took His servant by night from the inviolable mosque to the farthest mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed [c1]. The purpose given is to show him some of Our signs [c2]. He is the Hearing, the Seeing [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah has one sentence of praise, one of purpose and one that names God as the Hearing and the Seeing, all around a journey told in a single clause [c1][c2][c3]. It names no person, no vehicle, no duration and no time of the night [c1].
chapters.kids_md: God took His servant by night from one mosque to a farthest mosque [c1]. It was to show him some of God's signs [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah begins with glory to God before it states the journey, as the wording of the ayah shows [c1]. Another is that the journey's purpose is stated as showing signs [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the servant is; the ayah does not name him.
- Not established: how the journey was made, how long it took, whether it was bodily or in vision, or what the signs were that he was shown.
- Not established: what the farthest mosque was or where, beyond the ayah's words about blessed surroundings.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the servant, the starting place and the farthest mosque by name, the vehicle, the ascent, the meetings with earlier prophets and the date.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the night journey and on the ascent that later tradition links with it. None is used in this draft.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the names Jerusalem, Isra, Miraj and Buraq and the place of the farthest mosque.
The Arabic for the first mosque (a descriptive epithet) is rendered 'inviolable'; the common rendering is 'sacred'. A scholar should decide the wording.
Whether the journey was in body or in spirit was disputed by earlier scholars and the ayah does not settle it; this draft takes no side.
